items.title: Workflow lab: Turning context into a plan with Specs and the Figma agent
items.excerpt: Figma walks through a workflow in which Specs and the Figma agent hold the product context (requirements, decisions, constraints) next to the design, so the agent can turn it into an implementation plan and hand it to code.
items.rationale: Primary-source, step-by-step workflow for keeping requirements beside the design so the Figma agent can plan and hand off to code — usable tomorrow.

items.title: Claude has a new mobile design, too.
items.excerpt: Anthropic is rolling out a refreshed Claude mobile app with a bottom tab bar for chat, Projects, Code and Artifacts (iOS 26+ first), a day after OpenAI previewed a similar tab-bar redesign of ChatGPT; AI assistants are converging on the same app layout.
items.rationale: Shipped UI redesign that, with ChatGPT's same-week tab-bar test, shows AI assistant apps converging on one navigation pattern — a live reference for product designers (one card for the c5 cluster).

items.title: 에이바 스튜디오, 인기 출시 영상의 컷을 내 제품 화면으로
items.excerpt: Ava Studio released 'Launch Videos' (Nov 17), which analyses the shot order, cut lengths and camera moves of launch videos that went viral on X and rebuilds them with the user's own product screens; it runs as a plugin inside Claude Code and Codex.
items.rationale: New release that lets designers produce launch videos from proven cut structures with their own product screens, inside the coding agents they already use.

items.title: XJet launches AI-driven Atelier platform for bespoke jewelry
items.excerpt: XJet Atelier lets users describe a charm in a few words or upload a photo; AI tools generate and refine the design, show a 360-degree preview and send it to XJet's metal 3D printers in stainless steel or sterling silver.
items.rationale: New product launch taking text/photo prompts all the way to printed metal parts — a concrete prompt-to-fabrication pipeline for product designers.

items.title: This movie poster is one big AI slop Easter egg hunt
items.excerpt: The poster for 'Artificial', the Sam Altman/OpenAI film, is deliberately packed with AI-slop tells for viewers to spot; Fast Company reports it was made by humans as a marketing play.
items.rationale: Fresh design-culture moment: human designers deliberately faking AI-slop tells as a campaign device; assigned to design only by the run brief.
